provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets a colon after `sumpsit`, a semicolon after `effectum` and a colon before `ita nobis`; 1962 sets comma, colon and semicolon respectively; 1862 abbreviates the conclusion to the bare cue `Qui tecum etc.`; 1962 prints `Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.`; j-forms: 1862 `Judas`, `Jesus`; 1862 layer accent damage: `pomam` for `poenam`, `pramiium` for `praemium`, `crrore` for `errore`, `largto-tur` for `largiatur`. Corroboration: the same prayer stands in the 1862 a second time at lines 31274-31289 (Feria V in Coena Domini, printed p. 159) in a cleaner scan, and that second impression supplies every letterform damaged in this one.

propers.text: Ecce lignum Crucis, in quo salus mundi pependit. Omnes R. Venite, adoremus.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1862 prints `Ecce lignum Crucis, in quo salus mundi pependit. Chorus R. Venite adoremus.` with the same threefold repetition the 1962 keeps; the 1861 prints the Latin response `Venite adoremus` beside its own English, so the identity is visible inside the witness as well. The 1955 order moved the unveiling to three stations, which changes the ceremony and not these words. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

propers.name: Improperia
propers.text:
Partes quae ad singulos choros spectant, indicantur numeris 1 (chorus primus), et 2 (chorus secundus); quae autem ab utroque choro simul cantanda sunt, indicantur hoc modo: 1 et 2.

I

1 et 2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi! V. Quia eduxi te de terra Aegypti: parasti Crucem Salvatori tuo.

1

Hagios o Theos.

2

Sanctus Deus.

1

Hagios Ischyros.

2

Sanctus Fortis.

1

Hagios Athanatos, eleison himas.

2

Sanctus Immortalis, miserere nobis.

1 et 2

Quia eduxi te per desertum quadraginta annis, et manna cibavi te, et introduxi te in terram satis bonam: parasti Crucem Salvatori tuo.

1

Hagios o Theos.

2

Sanctus Deus.

1

Hagios Ischyros.

2

Sanctus Fortis.

1

Hagios Athanatos, eleison himas.

2

Sanctus Immortalis, miserere nobis.

1 et 2

Quid ultra debui facere tibi, et non feci? Ego quidem plantavi te vineam electam meam speciosissimam: et tu facta es mihi nimis amara: aceto namque sitim meam potasti, et lancea perforasti latus Salvatori tuo.

1

Hagios o Theos.

2

Sanctus Deus.

1

Hagios Ischyros.

2

Sanctus Fortis.

1

Hagios Athanatos, eleison himas.

2

Sanctus Immortalis, miserere nobis.

II

1

Ego propter te flagellavi Aegyptum cum primogenitis suis: et tu me flagellatum tradidisti.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego eduxi te de Aegypto, demerso Pharaone in Mare Rubrum: et tu me tradidisti principibus sacerdotum.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego ante te aperui mare: et tu aperuisti lancea latus meum.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego ante te praeivi in columna nubis: et tu me duxisti ad praetorium Pilati.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego te pavi manna per desertum: et tu me cecidisti alapis et flagellis.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego te potavi aqua salutis de petra: et tu me potasti felle et aceto.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego propter te Chananaeorum reges percussi: et tu percussisti arundine caput meum.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego dedi tibi sceptrum regale: et tu dedisti capiti meo spineam coronam.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

1

Ego te exaltavi magna virtute: et tu me suspendisti in patibulo Crucis.

2

Popule meus, quid feci tibi? Aut in quo contristavi te? Responde mihi!

III

1 et 2 Antiphona:

Crucem tuam adoramus, Domine, et sanctam resurrectionem tuam laudamus, et glorificamus: ecce enim propter lignum venit gaudium in universo mundo.

1 Psalmus 66, 2:

Deus misereatur nostri, et benedicat nobis.

2

Illuminet vultum suum super nos, et misereatur nostri.

1 et 2 Antiphona:

Crucem tuam adoramus, Domine, et sanctam resurrectionem tuam laudamus, et glorificamus: ecce enim propter lignum venit gaudium in universo mundo.

IV

1 et 2 Antiphona:

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine. Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

1 Hymnus:

Pange, lingua, gloriosi lauream certaminis, Et super Crucis trophaeo dic triumphum nobilem: Qualiter Redemptor orbis immolatus vicerit.

2

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine.

1

De parentis protoplasti fraude Factor condolens, Quando pomi noxialis in necem morsu ruit: Ipse lignum tunc notavit, damna ligni ut solveret.

2

Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

1

Hoc opus nostrae salutis ordo depoposcerat: Multiformis proditoris ars ut artem falleret, Et medelam ferret inde, hostis unde laeserat.

2

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine.

1

Quando venit ergo sacri plenitudo temporis, Missus est ab arce Patris Natus, orbis Conditor, Atque ventre virginali carne amictus prodiit.

2

Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

1

Vagit infans inter arcta conditus praesepia, Membra pannis involuta Virgo Mater alligat, Et Dei manus pedesque stricta cingit fascia.

2

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine.

1

Lustra sex qui iam peregit, tempus implens corporis, Sponte libera Redemptor passioni deditus, Agnus in Crucis levatur immolandus stipite.

2

Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

1

Felle potus ecce languet; spina, clavi, lancea Mite corpus perforarunt, unda manat et cruor; Terra, pontus, astra, mundus quo lavantur flumine!

2

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine.

1

Flecte ramos, arbor alta, tensa laxa viscera, Et rigor lentescat ille, quem dedit nativitas, Et superni membra Regis tende miti stipite.

2

Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

1

Sola digna tu fuisti ferre mundi victimam, Atque portum praeparare arca mundo naufrago, Quam sacer cruor perunxit, fusus Agni corpore.

2

Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis; Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine.

Conclusio numquam omittenda:

1

Sempiterna sit beatae Trinitati gloria; Aequa Patri Filioque, par decus Paraclito; Unius Trinique nomen laudet universitas. Amen.

2

Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet.

translations.text:
The parts belonging to each choir are marked by the numbers 1 (first choir) and 2 (second choir); those to be sung by both choirs together are marked in this way: 1 and 2.

I

1 and 2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me! V. Because I led you out of the land of Egypt, you prepared a Cross for your Savior.

1

Holy God.

2

Holy God.

1

Holy Mighty One.

2

Holy Mighty One.

1

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

2

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

1 and 2

Because I led you through the desert for forty years, fed you with manna, and brought you into a very good land, you prepared a Cross for your Savior.

1

Holy God.

2

Holy God.

1

Holy Mighty One.

2

Holy Mighty One.

1

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

2

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

1 and 2

What more ought I to have done for you that I have not done? I indeed planted you as my chosen, most beautiful vine; but you became exceedingly bitter to me: for you gave me vinegar to drink in my thirst, and with a lance pierced the side of your Savior.

1

Holy God.

2

Holy God.

1

Holy Mighty One.

2

Holy Mighty One.

1

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

2

Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.

II

1

For your sake I scourged Egypt with its firstborn; but you handed me over, scourged.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I led you out of Egypt, drowning Pharaoh in the Red Sea; but you handed me over to the chief priests.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I opened the sea before you; but you opened my side with a lance.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I went before you in a pillar of cloud; but you led me to Pilate’s praetorium.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I fed you with manna through the desert; but you struck me with slaps and scourges.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I gave you saving water from the rock to drink; but you gave me gall and vinegar to drink.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

For your sake I struck down the kings of the Canaanites; but you struck my head with a reed.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I gave you a royal scepter; but you gave my head a crown of thorns.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

1

I raised you up with great power; but you hung me on the gibbet of the Cross.

2

My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I saddened you? Answer me!

III

1 and 2 Antiphon:

We adore your Cross, Lord, and we praise and glorify your holy resurrection: for behold, through the wood joy has come throughout the world.

1 Psalm 66:2:

May God have mercy on us and bless us.

2

May he shine his face upon us and have mercy on us.

1 and 2 Antiphon:

We adore your Cross, Lord, and we praise and glorify your holy resurrection: for behold, through the wood joy has come throughout the world.

IV

1 and 2 Antiphon:

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit. Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

1 Hymn:

Sing, tongue, the laurel of the glorious contest, and over the trophy of the Cross proclaim the noble triumph: how the Redeemer of the world conquered by being sacrificed.

2

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit.

1

The Maker, grieving at the deception of our first-formed father, when by biting the harmful fruit he fell into death, himself then marked out the wood to undo the harm of the wood.

2

Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

1

The order of our salvation had called for this work: that craft might outwit the many-formed betrayer’s craft, and bring a remedy from where the enemy had wounded.

2

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit.

1

Therefore, when the fullness of the sacred time came, the Son, the Maker of the world, was sent from the Father’s citadel; and from a virgin’s womb he came forth clothed in flesh.

2

Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

1

The infant cries, laid within the narrow manger; the Virgin Mother binds his limbs wrapped in cloths, and a tight band encircles the hands and feet of God.

2

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit.

1

Having now passed thirty years, completing the span of his bodily life, the Redeemer freely gives himself to the Passion; the Lamb is lifted on the trunk of the Cross to be sacrificed.

2

Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

1

Behold, having drunk gall, he languishes; thorn, nails, and lance have pierced his gentle body; water and blood flow forth. In what a stream earth, sea, stars, and world are washed!

2

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit.

1

Bend your branches, tall tree; relax your taut fibers; let the stiffness given by your birth grow soft, and spread the limbs of the heavenly King upon a gentle trunk.

2

Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

1

You alone were worthy to bear the world’s victim and, as an ark, prepare a harbor for the shipwrecked world—you whom the sacred blood, poured from the Lamb’s body, anointed.

2

Faithful Cross, the one noble tree among them all; no forest brings forth its equal in leaf, flower, or fruit.

The conclusion is never to be omitted:

1

May eternal glory be to the blessed Trinity: equal glory to the Father and the Son, the same honor to the Paraclete. Let all creation praise the name of the One and Three. Amen.

2

Sweet the wood, sweet the nails; it bears a sweet weight.

propers.name: Antiphons at the Translation of the Blessed Sacrament
propers.text:
Adoramus te, Christe, et benedicimus tibi, quia per Crucem tuam redemisti mundum.

Per lignum servi facti sumus, et per sanctam Crucem liberati sumus: fructus arboris seduxit nos, Filius Dei redemit nos.

Salvator mundi, salva nos: qui per Crucem et Sanguinem tuum redemisti nos, auxiliare nobis, te deprecamur, Deus noster.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text:
We adore you, Christ, and we bless you, because by your Cross you redeemed the world.

By a tree we were made slaves, and by the holy Cross we were freed: the fruit of a tree led us astray, the Son of God redeemed us.

Savior of the world, save us: you who redeemed us by the Cross and your Blood, help us, we beg you, our God.

propers.incipit: Deus, Deus meus, respice in me
